minutes.headline: Select Board heard residents on 2023 lakefront tax assessment spikes and moved to open a charter investigation; vote result not captioned.
minutes.summary: After a short liquor-license hearing for a new restaurant, the meeting was a large public forum at the high school on sharply higher FY23 lakefront assessments. The principal assessor explained the mass-appraisal method and residents questioned him at length. The chair then moved to launch a Select Board investigation under the Town Charter, followed by public comment.

public_comment.topic: Suggested the assessment formula may violate Proposition 2.5 and urged contacting the attorney general; says own value rose after buying.
Read a statement about her elderly, ill veteran father facing a large tax increase on a fixed income.
Presented ten-year lake sales and land price statistics arguing land values were overstated.
Proposed a resolution stating no confidence in the assessment outcome and that individual abatements cannot fix it.
Compared actual land purchase prices on nearby lots with the assessed values and questioned decoupling land from building value.

public_comment.stated_role: reading a statement for a Hickory Hills resident
public_comment.topic: Statement from a 73-year-old on Social Security; asked for a senior cap on tax increases.
Asked for assurance that abatement applicants will be approved; officials said no outcome can be promised.
Suggested publishing the data used to build the assessments to improve transparency.
Asked why a site adjustment changed from last year on a property bought in 2019.
Complained about getting few town services for taxes paid; also raised light pollution.
Urged a quick fix, proposed paying the three-year average and skipping abatements, and warned of a class action and media attention.
Former select board member recalled 26 years of outsourced assessing with no such problem and urged revisiting that approach.
Described his assessment versus a bank appraisal and asked for evenly distributed, fair assessments.
Announced a Saturday abatement help workshop at Andrews Hall with realtors.
Argued waterfront owners were singled out when the town could have spread taxes across all property.

votes.motion: Approve the all-alcohol restaurant license, common victualler license and weekday/Sunday entertainment license for La Bella Restaurante.

Under section 3-2e of the Town Charter, the Select Board conducts an investigation into effects of COVID-19 on 2021 property values, the FY23 assessments, and the valuation and billing process; chair leads with the vice chair and town manager.

budget_items.what_was_said: Town meeting appropriated an overlay amount, but assessors can grant abatements beyond it; a higher cumulative level is where the town budget is affected.
A board member said every abatement reduces town revenue and could total millions, affecting capital and services.
The chair explained the town budget can grow only by the statutory percentage plus new growth absent an override.

budget_items.topic: Outside appraisers and staffing for abatements
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager will post RFPs for outside assessors and seek staffing agency help for the assessor's office.
A board member noted residents may pay for private appraisals to support abatement applications.

decisions.decision: Officials advised residents they need not pay more than a formula-based amount by Feb 1 to preserve abatement rights; worksheets to be provided and posted on the town website.
Town manager to issue RFPs for outside assessors and arrange administrative staffing for the assessor's office, with support in place by late February or March 1.
Board to publish an answer on the town website about whether abatement applicants may add information after Feb 1.
Public comment was consolidated to the end of the agenda.
Next steps are to finalize a roadmap and timeline for the investigation and give residents routine updates.

what_happened.line: The Select Board moved to open an investigation under section 3-2e of the Town Charter into the FY23 assessments and the valuation and billing process; the vote was not captioned.
Officials told residents they need not pay more than a formula-based amount by Feb 1 to preserve abatement rights, with worksheets to be posted on the town website.
The town manager is to issue requests for proposals for outside assessors and arrange staffing for the assessor's office, with support in place by late February or March 1.
The principal assessor explained the mass-appraisal method, and residents questioned the assessors and board at length.
Public comment, moved to the end of the agenda, included requests for a senior cap and a resolution of no confidence in the assessment outcome.

why_it_matters: Lakefront owners facing sharply higher FY23 assessments have a Feb 1 payment point tied to abatement rights, and abatements granted beyond the overlay reduce town revenue and can touch the town budget, mostly taxes.

The charter investigation and outside assessors may change how the valuation and billing process is run, and the open question of whether abatement applicants can add information after Feb 1 affects every applicant.
watch_next: The board's roadmap and timeline for the charter investigation, and routine updates to residents.
The town website answer on whether abatement applicants may add information after Feb 1, and the outside-assessor requests for proposals.
